statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-55467 (GHSA-69qc-prxg-h2c7): before CUPS 2.4.20, the scheduler copies the destination-uri and pre-dial-string values of a fax job into the phone and faxPrefix filter options without the control-character filter that other job options get, so a user who can submit a job can inject control characters into the filter options. The upstream fix copies both values through a buffer that replaces control characters and DEL with spaces, in get_options() in scheduler/job.c: https://github.com/OpenPrinting/cups/security/advisories/GHSA-69qc-prxg-h2c7 and commit 0cf4e7814d6810ed3c454222bce3aa342d541681 on the 2.4.x branch, first released in 2.4.20: https://github.com/OpenPrinting/cups/commit/0cf4e7814d6810ed3c454222bce3aa342d541681. We downloaded every package built from the cups source in the Alpine 3.23 index of the DHI Alpine repository, for x86_64 and aarch64 (cups, cups-client, cups-dbg, cups-dev, cups-doc, cups-lang, cups-libs, cups-openrc and ipptool at 2.4.13-r0, 2.4.16-r0, 2.4.18-r0 and 2.4.18-r1; 72 apks), checked each against its index checksum, and disassembled the code in /usr/sbin/cupsd that adds the phone and faxPrefix options; the compiler inlines get_options() into cupsdContinueJob(), which we located with the symbol table in cups-dbg. In 2.4.13-r0, 2.4.16-r0 and 2.4.18-r0, on both architectures, cupsd passes the destination-uri value after its tel: prefix, and the pre-dial-string value, straight to cupsAddOption(). In 2.4.18-r1, on both architectures, each value is first copied into a 256-byte stack buffer by a loop that replaces bytes below 0x20 and DEL (0x7f) with a space, and cupsAddOption() receives that buffer, which is the upstream fix. 2.4.18-r1 is the first build that carries it.

CVE-2026-55467 (GHSA-69qc-prxg-h2c7): before CUPS 2.4.20, the scheduler copies the destination-uri and pre-dial-string values of a fax job into the phone and faxPrefix filter options without the control-character filter that other job options get, so a user who can submit a job can inject control characters into the filter options. The upstream fix copies both values through a buffer that replaces control characters and DEL with spaces, in get_options() in scheduler/job.c: https://github.com/OpenPrinting/cups/security/advisories/GHSA-69qc-prxg-h2c7 and commit 0cf4e7814d6810ed3c454222bce3aa342d541681 on the 2.4.x branch, first released in 2.4.20: https://github.com/OpenPrinting/cups/commit/0cf4e7814d6810ed3c454222bce3aa342d541681. We downloaded every package built from the cups source in the DHI Debian repository for trixie, amd64 and arm64, including the -dbgsym packages: 22 binary packages in each of the four published DHI builds of 2.4.10-3+deb13u2, the fifth to the eighth (176 debs), each checked against its index checksum; the earlier DHI builds are no longer published. Debian lists the CVE as open for trixie, with no fixed version, at https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-55467, so its own 2.4.10-3+deb13u2 packages serve as the unfixed comparison. We disassembled the code in /usr/sbin/cupsd (cups-daemon) that adds the phone and faxPrefix options, in the DHI builds and in Debian's packages; the compiler inlines get_options() into cupsdContinueJob(), which we located with the symbol tables in the -dbgsym packages. In Debian's build and in the fifth, sixth and seventh DHI builds, on both architectures, cupsd passes the destination-uri value after its tel: prefix, and the pre-dial-string value, straight to cupsAddOption(). In the eighth DHI build, on both architectures, each value is first copied into a 256-byte stack buffer by a loop that replaces bytes below 0x20 and DEL (0x7f) with a space, and cupsAddOption() receives that buffer, which is the upstream fix backported to 2.4.10. The eighth DHI build of 2.4.10-3+deb13u2 is the first that carries it.
